reviews.review: I recommend this with a caveat. I'm playing it right before the devs overhaul the mana system to be very different than it currently is. They must have gotten a bunch of a feedback about how it was dogwater or something, because the new system is VERY different, and I don't actually think its better. That being said, the new system is also fine, just less interesting. Both systems are interesting enough that it shows the devs have real design chops, and despite being a genuine EA game (bugs are present, work is being done etc etc) its a lot of fun. Maybe wait for a sale if you don't want to pay for an unfinished game, or wait for launch. Good luck devs!

Northwind does something completely different with its core gameplay compared to most entries in the genre, leading to a very unique experience. The biggest divergences from most other games in the genre are as follows:

 - Most of the resources (e.g. mana, block, many status effects) persist from one turn to the next
 - Mana is generated by drawing specific resource generating cards rather than you gaining a fixed amount each turn
 - There's a level up mechanic where you can expend mana to power up most of your cards for the rest of the fight
 - Your attack and defense are fundamentally one and the same, with your accumulated attack value for the turn being compared against the enemy's to determine who takes damage and how much (block, mentioned earlier, is more of a long term defensive mechanic that isn't nearly as easy to get as it is in a lot of games in the genre).

All of this makes the battles somewhat slower, with a distinct early, middle and late game and a corresponding focus on long term planning and resource management. Due to this, most battles feel winnable with proper decision making and defeats feel like a consequence of bad resource management or a poorly constructed deck (which can, admittedly, be thanks to a poor selection of cards to draft, like in any deckbuilder). 

Besides all of this, they've done a number of changes to the surrounding gameplay systems, which serve to either improve on some genre staples or, at the very least, change up the formula:

- Consumables have been replaced with perks, which are generally slightly less powerful but can be reused each battle. No more dying while trying to save the potion for a later battle.
- Each act is shorter, usually consisting of three to four enemy encounters and three to four other events (this is pretty important since each fight takes longer due to how combat works).
- The map for each act has been streamlined considerably, so that instead of trying to plan a route through the entire act at the start you are essentially choosing from a series of forks.
- Most card upgrading is done in a between act town area, with a gem socketing system that allows for a lot of flexibility in how you empower your cards.
- Instead of getting a random boss each act from a pool for that act, each run you fight a progressively harder version of the boss you select in act 1. This has its pros and cons, but I personally find it satisfying being able to tailor my build to be able to deal with the monster I'm hunting down for the run.

As far as the amount of content in the game goes, as of this writing there are currently two characters that play quite differently from each other. They both have several distinct builds that can work and, taken together with the gem socketing mentioned earlier, I rarely feel like I'm doing the same thing from one run to the next.

All that being said, the game isn't without its flaws, most of which come down to balance or performance and will hopefully be fixed through early access. Notably:
- Enemy encounters vary wildly in difficulty. Some normal encounters feel harder than most of the elite encounters and some elite encounters feel harder than a lot of the bosses.
- If you get a REALLY big deck (maybe 40-50 cards?) the game slows down any time you need to shuffle/look through it.
- While perks and gems are broken up into two different tiers, even within a tier there's a lot of variation in how strong they are, with some upgrades feeling borderline useless compared to others.
- You can fuse duplicates of cards together to ostensibly make them more powerful, but many of these "upgrades" feel more like...sidegrades, or sometimes even downgrades.
- There's currently no inspection feature for the cards, meaning you don't know what the fused version will look like until you actually go to do it (worth noting that they explicitly list an inspection feature as something they'll be adding in their roadmap, so I expect this will be fixed later).

All in all, if you like roguelike deckbuilders, or have been wanting to give them a try, and are looking for something different, I strongly recommend Northwind.

I want to like this game, but it has some serious balance issues. You are already handicapped by this games mana system and having to save or use so you can level, which wouldn't be a bad thing if the enemies(including elites and normal not even just bosses) couldn't hit you for 50+ on turn 1 or turn 2. Your not even given enough time to build any mana economy to even defend yourself or counteract that kind of damage. It also wouldn't be so bad if it was just for one turn, but if you survive they come back the next turn with 40+ dmg attack and the next turn with 50+ dmg attack. What sense does that make. Granted you will run into this from act 2 forward not so much act 1. This is all without upping the hazard mode. So I can only imagine the levels of imbalance once you up it. I've played plenty of roguelike deckbuilders from sts, monster train, bb, spellrogue, bazaar and balatro to name a few. Obviously some are pvp more than pve, but there is a range balance of fun and difficulty to just ridiculous imbalance. The perk system needs to be revamped to once per turn because once per combat is literally pointless.

小号玩了一把，纯💩
1.压制牌的描述跟弱智一样，被压制时生效，看起来就像我要被压才能生效，翻译成压制敌人时生效会杀了翻译组的🐴吗？

2.内容过少，就打了一把，第一图跟第二图的精英和BOSS全是同一个，就是加了数值跟机制，不是，大哥，72块钱的游戏，一张图就1个BOSS1个精英你还能整换皮啊？合着你们就做了1个精英跟1个BOSS的立绘呗

3.游戏机制纯💩 这游戏攻击跟防御整合到了一起，用我方攻击力扣敌人攻击力，举个例子，敌人打我10 我打敌人12，那么合起来就是我打敌人2，反过来就会挨打，然后这游戏加能量的方式是抽能量牌，而能量牌的攻击力是很低的，这就导致如果你想出牌，就得抓能量牌，而抓了能量牌，就等于你鬼抽，然后这游戏因为统合了攻击跟防御，怪物跟超雄一样，第一张图还装模作样，第二张图直接每回合30-60的攻击要求，注意！攻击要求不是攻击值，因为这游戏敌人会有防御，但是你以为它是空过吗？错误的，防御值＞你的攻击值就给你严重的debuff，要么就塞牌，也就是说，你必须每回合都打30+的平均输出才行，那问题来了，你要出牌，是不是要费用？而你抽了能量牌，就＝鬼抽，这游戏虽然能量可以留到下一回合，但是，因为每回合都有的高压输出需求，就导致能量牌少＝出不来牌直接死，能量牌多＝必定有一回合鬼抽然后被血入，
   重！点！来！了！    还记得我之前说的，这游戏的伤害的我方攻击数值减去敌方防御/攻击数值吗？而敌人第二图每回合数值都是30-60之间，也就是说哪怕你每个回合都有均40+的输出，敌人哪怕取最小值30，你也就打他10点血，一个100血的敌人哪怕你无限能量都要这样磨10个回合！！！但你抽卡不可能不抽能量牌加费出牌，而加了费就＝鬼抽，但凡你鬼抽1回合就被血入，被敌人上一堆debuff，因为debuff攻击力不够，然后崩盘！😄😄😄😄😄

4.宣传欺诈，宣传当时可是说了能捉宠物，“卡牌类的怪物猎人”，不懂就问抓宠在哪？怪猎在哪？

我真艹了这逆天出生游戏，内容少机制💩数值烂，小精英一回合打60真给我逗笑了，2图的BOSS跟精英加起来就2个立绘，杀戮尖塔1层精英都有3个呢我艹你的，你两个图精英BOSS就2个，然后机制纯💩，但凡不天胡就只能磨血折磨自己，然后宣传欺诈，2个角色出门就这还敢卖72块钱，赶紧死吧我说真的🙏🏻别来害人了，已退款

哦对了，塞牌怪塞的牌会封住你左右两边的牌不能用，你必须花1费打出debuff牌才能用，而这个debuff牌是没有像杀戮尖塔那样的消耗的，换句话说就是1费不消耗还带封牌的粘液，然后结合我上面说的：
1.每回合抽牌珍贵，抽能量牌＝鬼抽，抽debuff牌＝倒扣能量
 2.超长线作战，每回合只能钝刀割肉扣几滴十几滴血，导致必然被大量塞牌
3.2反过来影响1，鬼抽导致攻击力不够被塞，塞了攻击力更加不够，恶性循环

这游戏你就玩吧，一玩一个不吱声，享受👍🏻

非常感谢您的反馈！

关于“压制”的翻译问题我们已经注意到——本地化团队会进一步核查，非常感谢您的指出。
我们计划在未来增加更多内容，但售价不会提高。关于当前的定价，我们认同您提到的观点，会重新审视定价的合理性。后续若有调整，我们会及时告知，再次感谢您提出这个宝贵意见。
我们也会针对这一机制的平衡问题进行调整，我们注意到部分技能和怪物的表现确实可能让人感觉不太公平。
游戏的主题是“怪物狩猎”，而不是捕捉宠物的怪物猎人，很抱歉宣传文案引起误解。我们计划在之后的内容中加入与怪物狩猎相关的要素——例如哨站第五个建筑「魔装工程师（Monster Gear Engineer）」，将在后续版本中推出。

最后，再次感谢您花时间撰写如此详细的评价！您的反馈让我们更清楚地了解问题所在，也帮助我们持续改进游戏体验。我们会继续努力，完善您提到的各个方面，真心感谢您的支持与关注！

再次感谢！

reviews.review: Great game.  In around 9 runs, I haven't run into any balance issues like a couple of negative reviews had referenced.   I constantly feel like each run is challenging, yet beatable, starting with the very first run.  The game might feel extra hard for people who aren't good at managing mana in Magic the Gathering; I was a pro player in Magic years ago, so it may be that I have an affinity for this game that some people won't have, but for me it feels perfect.  I love the innovations in this game vs Slay the Spire clones.  I like the combat clash instead of block/attack cards.  I love the leveling up idea and implementation.  I love what you can do at each Outpost.  I pretty much always feel like the gold/bones/scales resources are tight, which means meaningful decisions.

原评论：战斗速度过于慢，使用一张牌卡顿一下太难受了

鉴于开发者可能误会了我的意思那我这里解释一下，我是开启了加速模式的，这个游戏目前最大的问题是动画演出上开启了加速模式后还需要每一张牌一两秒的动画观看时间，并且这段时间内我无法进行任何操作，这就导致了我打一张牌等一下打一张牌等一下这个非常不好的游戏体验。

另游戏目前还有其他缺点：
1.目前的数值平衡很差；
2.游戏内查看升级卡牌是很费劲的，鼠标左右键的操作是一致的；
3.游戏内的敌对生物种类没有太明确的机制区分，对于目前的我来说就是一路莽，没有对策可言。
